TWO HYPOTHESES RESOLVED FROM DATA ALREADY ON DISK, no device time spent:
  A) **Hypothesis 4 (recall thoughts) is FALSIFIED -- do not run it.** Its own precondition was
     "reader values a recall span >= +2 nats". runs/probes/recall_r24_3800.json (sitting unread
     since 2026-09-14) says the best-overlap context span scores -3.09, WORSE than a random
     context span (-2.69) and 2 nats worse than an empty thought (-0.97); mean content-token
     overlap only 4.0 of 16. It misses by 5 nats. Queue entry rewritten to say so.
  B) **"The reader ignores thoughts" is WRONG, and the distinction matters.** ob0 ~ 0 says
     shuffling a thought's tokens is free, but feeding run 26's filler-trained reader a real
     written thought costs ~-10 to -13 nats. So the reader conditions VERY strongly on what
     register occupies the slot and not at all on token ORDER within it: it reads a thought as
     a bag of words, never as a sequence. Stop writing "the reader ignores them".
THE CENTRAL FACT, everything on one nats-over-silence scale (now §2 of SUPERVISOR.md):
    perfect 16-token future hint  +11.0   |  content-free filler        ~0
    own written thought            -1.2   |  in-context recall span     -3.1
    random context span            -2.7
  The reader has enormous unused appetite for real future information, and EVERY content source
  we can produce at inference is worse than silence. That is the bottleneck -- not calibration,
  not reward shaping. Judge new hypotheses on whether they plausibly produce positive-value
  CONTENT, not on whether they raise g.
  => Promoted to queue #5 the one untested inference-available content source: **self-forecast
  thoughts** (the model's own greedy continuation of the window as the thought). Learnable by
  construction (self-distillation, not an unreachable oracle) and actually about the future.
  Probe it cheaply FIRST via a `self16` condition in probe_oracle_offset.py on the calibrated
  run-25 checkpoint. If it does not clear the filler floor as a HINT, no writer trained toward
  it can help, and that closes the approach with a clean negative result.

### 2. Queue #5 (self-forecast) probed cheaply, as the runbook asked -- and it FAILS its floor.
Added to probe_oracle_offset.py (backup /tmp/probe_oracle_offset.py.bak2, py_compile OK, both new
conditions OFF by default so the old invocation is byte-for-byte unchanged):
  `self16` (4th arg): the model's own greedy prediction of the window, spliced as the thought,
    taken TEACHER-FORCED (argmax at clean row n+j, conditioned on the true prefix). Not available
    at inference, so it is an UPPER BOUND on any free-running self-forecast a writer could be
    trained toward. The point of the bound: if the upper bound fails, queue #5 closes for the
    cost of one forward instead of a run.
  `mix<K>` (5th arg, the PRECISION LADDER): the true hint with only K of 12 tokens kept IN THEIR
    TRUE POSITIONS, the rest replaced by tokens drawn from this sequence's own earlier context --
    register-correct, content-wrong, i.e. what an imperfect forecast looks like.
SMOKE ONLY, n=37, one sequence per domain -- DO NOT QUOTE, the full n=465 run is in flight:
  o0 +12.43  o8 +13.28  o16 +12.71  o24 +10.17  o32 +8.07  o48 +4.59  o64 +0.22
  shuf0 +1.86  shuf64 -0.08  silence_ctl +0.04  pause_ctl -0.03
  self16 -0.89      (SET overlap 5.73/12, POSITIONAL accuracy 4.46/12)
  mix2 +0.17  mix4 +0.54  mix6 +1.77  mix8 +3.31  mix10 +7.09  mix12 +12.43
**TWO FINDINGS, and the second one reframes the programme.**
(a) BREAK-EVEN IS 2/12. Two positionally-correct tokens out of twelve already beat the filler
    floor. The bar for a useful thought is far LOWER than eight runs of failure suggested. It was
    never "be accurate"; the reader pays generously for a trickle of real future content.
(b) AT MATCHED ACCURACY THE MODEL'S OWN FORECAST IS ~1.4 NATS WORSE THAN NOISE. self16 is
    positionally right 4.46/12 and scores -0.89; mix4 is positionally right 4/12 and scores +0.54.
    Same amount of truth, opposite sign. So the penalty is NOT the forecast's inaccuracy -- it is
    WHAT THE MODEL WRITES WHEN IT IS WRONG. Greedy argmax errors are confident, high-frequency,
    plausible tokens the reader treats as evidence; random context tokens are visibly noise it
    discounts. This is the same mechanism as run 26's -10 nats for a real thought fed to a
    filler-trained reader: the reader is exquisitely sensitive to the DISTRIBUTION in the slot.
    Consequence if it survives n=465: the programme's problem is not writer accuracy, it is that
    a confident wrong thought is worse than no thought, and every objective we have run rewards
    confidence. That is a publishable reframing and it points at a different intervention
    (calibrated/abstaining thoughts, or noise-shaped errors) than anything in the queue.
CAVEAT I am holding myself to: n=37 on one smoke, and self16 is teacher-forced (optimistic).
  Nothing above goes in the paper until the n=465 run lands.

FOUR things follow, and I am correcting two of this journal's own earlier claims.
(i) **THE READER IS NOT ORDER-BLIND -- I retract that wording** (04:07 and 02:07 ticks, and it
    had reached SUPERVISOR.md S2 and the paper). Shuffling a REAL hint costs 10.5 of its 10.7
    nats. ob0 ~ 0 is a fact about OUR WRITERS, not about the reader: their thoughts contain
    nothing whose order could matter. We measured the writer and blamed the reader.
(ii) **"Break-even is 2/12" (04:07 tick) is WRONG** -- that was an n=37 smoke whose filler floor
    was off by 0.7 nats. Break-even is ~4/12 (mix4 sits ON the floor, mix6 is +0.97 above it).
    It never reached the paper. The encouraging direction survives: 4/12 is still a far lower
    bar than eight runs of failure suggested.
(iii) **Queue #5 (self-forecast) is CLOSED by its own upper bound.** self16 - filler = -0.61, and
    self16 is TEACHER-FORCED, i.e. an upper bound no free-running writer can reach. Finding (b)
    from 04:07 SURVIVES at n=458: self16 is right 5.30/12 yet scores 1.2 nats BELOW the ladder
    rung at that accuracy (interpolating mix4/mix6 gives ~-0.11 against the observed -1.35).
    Confident wrong tokens get believed; context-drawn wrong tokens get discounted.
(iv) **THE NEW FACT, and it is the most useful number this project has produced.** The writer's
    free-running thought agrees with the true continuation on **4% of tokens**, falling to 2% at
    m=12. The same model's teacher-forced argmax is right ~44%. The writer is not a bad
    forecaster -- it is not forecasting at all. And the damage is monotone in length: truncating
    its own thought to 2 tokens nearly recovers the filler floor.
**THE CAUSE IS IN OUR OWN CONFIGS.** Runs 24-27 all ran `--oracle-min-off 8 --oracle-max-off 48`.
Run 24 chose that to exclude "the trivial copy of the immediate continuation (speculative
decoding)". Per the ladder, o48 is +2.9 and o64 is -0.9: tokens that far ahead are near

### 5. THE NEXT HYPOTHESIS, proposed here BEFORE implementing, as the 06:07 tick required.
If run 28 fails, the ladder points at **abstention**, not at another reward shape. The two facts
are: filler in the slot costs ~0, and a confident wrong token costs more than noise. So let the
writer emit the FILLER token at positions it is not confident about and commit only where it is.
It needs a precondition probe first, and the probe is cheap (CPU, no device time):
  (i) `pmixK` in probe_oracle_offset.py: K true tokens in TRUE positions, the rest filled with
      the PAUSE token instead of context noise. If its break-even is below mix's ~4/12, the idea
      is alive. Caveat the probe exists to settle: interleaved pause is out of distribution for a
      reader trained on a `[SPACE]*N + [T_CLOSE]` prefix BLOCK, so it may score badly for a
      reason that training would fix -- read a bad pmix result as "needs a mixed-fill reader",
      not as "abstention is dead".
  (ii) `selfconfC`: the self-forecast keeping only the C most confident positions, pause
      elsewhere; report precision@C. This is the number that decides everything -- if the model's
      own confidence does not select correct positions, no abstention scheme can work.
Do NOT launch an abstention run before (i) and (ii) land. Mind G24 when editing that file.

### 2. G26: the success bar is a DIFFERENCE, and the probe was throwing away the pairing.
The +-0.148 above is CONSERVATIVE and unnecessarily so. `probe_thinkmode.py` wrote only
mean/se/n, so own-vs-`--pause` could only be combined as if the two runs were independent. They
are not: the traversal is deterministic (fixed domains, fixed `eval_batches`, fixed NPER; with
`--pause` the generator is never called at all, so the rng cannot desynchronise it), so both runs
score THE SAME ANCHORS IN THE SAME ORDER. Anchor difficulty is the dominant variance component,
so the paired se should be much smaller -- and the bar is exactly the number that decides runs.

every existing key is untouched, so nothing that reads the old JSONs changes. Compiled, and

### 3. I am RETRACTING the imCE test I pre-registered at 08:07. It was a badly posed test.
At 08:07 I wrote: "Run 27 reached imCE 1.85 by step 800; if run 28 has not fallen at least that
far by step 800, the writer is not learning to forecast either." That comparison is meaningless
and I should not have written it. **Imitation CE is the CE of a DIFFERENT TARGET in each run**, so
a lower value is not a better writer -- it is a more predictable target. Run 28's target is the
span at offset 0-4, which is essentially ordinary next-token prediction relocated into the thought
block, and its entropy floor is the model's own NTP entropy. The numbers:
    run 27 (offsets 8-48): imCE 2.79 -> 2.03 -> 1.58 -> flat ~1.7,   its ntp1 ~2.75
    run 28 (offsets  0-4): imCE 4.19 -> 3.70 -> 3.41 -> flat ~3.45,  its ntp1 ~2.78
Read correctly this is the opposite of alarming in one respect and a real question in another.
(a) Run 28's imCE plateaued within 100 steps at ~0.65 ABOVE its own ntp1 -- which is about what
    the jitter over 5 unknown offsets is worth. The writer can already produce this target
    teacher-forced; there was little for it to learn, which is why it converged in 100 steps.
(b) Run 27's imCE sat more than a nat BELOW the model's own NTP entropy on general text. A target
    a model predicts far better than it predicts text is a target with a narrow, stereotyped
    distribution -- which is a restatement, in the training log, of the register collapse the
    probes found. I now read run 27's "good" imCE as a symptom, not a strength.
Neither (a) nor (b) tells us whether the FREE-RUNNING thought carries the content: imCE is
teacher-forced, and the whole lesson of the draft probe is that this model's teacher-forced
argmax is right 44% of the time while its free-running thought is right 4%. So I replaced the
retracted test with the direct instrument, below.

most useful arithmetic the project has done.** Every selfconfC is BELOW the filler floor

    C     prec@C    p*     short by
    2     0.813   0.969     0.156
    4     0.713   0.794     0.081
    6     0.637   0.697     0.060
    8     0.559   0.611     0.052

**Uniformly short, never over, and the shortfall shrinks as the writer speaks more.** At twelve
tokens we are under three points of precision from a useful thought. But self16 is TEACHER-FORCED.
The free-running writer agrees on 11% of tokens where the teacher-forced one is right 44%.
Abstention buys 0.03-0.16 of precision headroom; **the free-running gap is 0.33.** Fix the big one
first. Abstention is kept in reserve as the right FORMAT to adopt later, already implemented.
(Caveat on p*: linear interpolation in precision at fixed C. The ladder is convex in K, so treat
p* as an estimate of the right size, not a measurement. It is stated as such in the paper.)

### 3. RUN 28 HAD AN ARITHMETIC BUG IN ITS OWN FLAGS, and I found it in our config, not by guessing.
`--oracle-mode jitter --oracle-min-off 0 --oracle-max-off 4` draws a fresh o ~ U{0..4} PER ANCHOR
(`think_train.py` ~line 385) and supervises the writer on x[n+1+o ...], while the REWARD always
scores the window starting at x[n+1]. The writer cannot observe o. A writer betting optimally on
offset 0 is right at most 0.44 x 0.2 = **0.088** of the time on the token actually scored.
**Run 28 measured 0.113.** The observed ceiling is what the jitter predicts, to within noise.
Second, independent trace in the training log: run 28's imCE plateaued inside 100 steps at 3.48
against its own ntp1 of 2.78 -- an excess of +0.70 nats that never came down. That is an
irreducible-ambiguity floor, not a learning curve. (log 5 = 1.61 if the five candidates were
disjoint and equiprobable; they overlap heavily, so +0.70 is the right size.)
Four runs excluded the immediate continuation as a "trivial copy"; the fifth finally aimed at it
and hid it behind a five-way lottery.

smoked at n=39 before the full run). `runs/probes/tfslot_r25_900.json`, run 25 @900, **n=616**, all
three columns from the SAME anchors and the SAME forward pass:
    prefix m     ntp   tfslot     own     per position i = 0..15:
          1    0.433   0.047   0.047   ntp     .43 .41 .43 .45 .44 .45 .43 .45 .46 .47 .45 .46 ...
          2    0.421   0.155   0.041   tfslot  .05 .26 .34 .37 .39 .42 .41 .40 .32 .31 .29 .31 ...
          4    0.429   0.255   0.035   own     .05 .03 .03 .03 .03 .03 .02 .01 .01 .00 .01 .01 ...
          8    0.437   0.330   0.029
         12    0.444   0.322   0.022

Two calibration checks, both passed before I read anything into it: `ntp` is flat at 0.43-0.47,
reproducing the central ladder's 0.442 from an independent instrument; and tfslot[0] == own[0]
exactly (0.047), which it MUST, because at position 0 the thought prefix is empty and the two
conditions are literally the same row. That identity is the probe's built-in alignment test.
**Given a true prefix the slot forecasts at 0.42 by position 5 -- indistinguishable from the base
model's 0.44 -- and averages 0.347 over positions 1-11, where the free-running thought scores
0.019. Break-even against the filler floor is 2/12 = 0.167 with pause padding. The capability is
present and ABOVE the bar; the decoding regime alone destroys it.** Two compounding parts:
  (1) position 0 is broken on its own -- the `<T>` row attends to exactly what clean row n attends
      to and scores 0.047 against 0.433, a 9x collapse BEFORE any self-conditioning is possible;
  (2) nothing recovers from it -- 0.347 teacher-forced vs 0.019 free over positions 1-11.
Before running it I cleared the two mechanical suspects by READING `think_par.py`, not guessing:
both samplers do `if r == spec_row: argmax` (l.209, l.249), so the greedy thought gets no top-k, no
freq-pen, no repeat ban, no temperature -- every "own greedy" number we have ever reported is a
plain argmax; and the penalty the SAMPLED rows do carry would block only 0.46% of true continuation
tokens (measured, n=232 spans, 3712 positions). Decoding was not the cause; the policy was.

### 3. The consequence, written down as queue #10 before the next tick can water it down.
`--imit-w 1.0` fills the thought block with the TRUE continuation, i.e. pure teacher forcing. **We
have trained the regime that works and never the regime we sample in, in every run of this project.**
Run 30 = scheduled sampling / DAgger: build the imitation block from the model's OWN sampled prefix
while keeping the true continuation as the CE target, ramp own-prefix probability 0 -> ~0.8, and
treat position 0 explicitly (a prefix ramp alone may not fix an opener that is broken at 0.047).

step 600, against 0.019. Judge it by that, NOT by g_r0/gSp/imCE -- it is a fixed instrument against
true held-out text and cannot rise with its own shuffle. This does NOT displace run 29: run 29 has
passed its own K1 and its K2 is registered at step 800.

### 2. Run 30 implemented (mechanism only -- NOT launched, NOT smoked).
`think_train.py`, backup kept at `think_train.py.bak_pre_ss_20260918`. New flags, **all default-off
so the old behaviour is bit-identical** (`ss_p = sched(...) = 0.0` makes the branch unreachable):
  `--ss-start 0.0 --ss-end 0.0 --ss-t0 0 --ss-t1 600 --ss-row {sample,spec}`
Per SSL anchor and per position, with probability ss_p, the block's INPUT token becomes the model's
OWN token while the CE TARGET stays the true continuation (DAgger: own states, expert labels):
    content_in = content.copy(); content_in[m_ss] = src[m_ss]
    buf = build_buffer(..., content_in, ...)      # input:  own tokens spliced in
    tgt = build_targets(..., content)             # target: UNCHANGED, the true continuation
Three design points, each for a reason rather than a default:
  - **Per-position Bernoulli (Bengio et al. 2015), not whole-prefix replacement.** With most
    positions still true the target x[n+1+t] stays identifiable, so the model learns to RECOVER
    from its own errors instead of being asked to predict a continuation it can no longer locate.
  - **Substitution stops at the source thought's own `</T>`**, so a stop token is never spliced into
    the middle of a block.
  - **ZERO extra device compute.** I checked rather than assumed: `gen.generate` returns z as
    [R+1, N, L] over ALL anchors including the SSL ones (think_par.py l.353, l.374), so the own
    tokens are already in hand. The runbook's queue #10 budgeted "one extra generate pass"; it is
    not needed. No new graph shape.
Verification, all four: `py_compile` OK; `test_rollouts.py` **ALL PASSED** (rollouts + soft-gate +
curriculum + mixed-anchor); a standalone splice check asserting targets are untouched, only SSL
block rows move, kept positions stay true, substituted positions carry no `</T>`, and ss_p=0 is a
no-op -- ALL PASSED; and the substitution RATE verified at scale (n=4000: 0.297 and 0.803 measured
for ss_p 0.3 and 0.8). `metrics.jsonl` gains `ss_p` and `ss_sub`; status.py selects keys by name so
the extra fields are inert. Run 29 is unaffected -- its ranks hold the old module, and a keepalive
relaunch would take the defaults, which are the old behaviour.

  pathway, and that pathway is what degrades. Same family as run 28's offset lottery.
  => **G30: before building a training signal, ask whether a PERFECT model could reach zero loss
  on it.** If not, the residue is noise on shared weights.

### 3. RUN 32, and why it is NOT another writer-accuracy run.
Since accuracy is a floor, run 32 attacks the COST term, which is larger and which we have measured
three times without ever acting on it: a confident wrong token is more expensive than a blank slot
(self16 is right 5.30/12 and scores 1.2 nats BELOW the mix rung at its own accuracy; run 28 RAISED
agreement 0.042 -> 0.113 and its own-filler gap got WORSE at every length). The writer emits ~12
confident tokens of which ~10.9 are wrong and pays for all of them.
MECHANISM, new flag `--abstain-mode freq` (default "none" = runs 13-31 bit-identical; trainer backup
`think_train.py.bak_pre_abstain_20260919_0607`, diff is 5 additive sites): in the imitation block the
TRUE token survives only where it is a top-300 unigram, every other position becomes SPACE, and `</T>`
padding past the thought's own end is untouched so lengths and the stop action are unchanged. I measured
the coverage rather than assuming it: **top-300 = 55% of the next-12 tokens on the val mixture, so the
supervised thought holds ~6.6 content positions and ~5.4 silences** (top-100 46%, top-200 53%).
WHY A UNIGRAM MASK AND NOT A CONFIDENCE HEAD: model-free, so zero extra forwards, and -- the actual
point -- it applies IDENTICALLY to the block INPUT and the CE TARGET because both derive from
`orc_content`. That regime-match is what run 30 bought with an extra generate pass and lost 0.013 of
own(1-11) doing. WHY THE FORMAT: the abstention ladder already measured interleaved pause as READABLE
(pmix2 -0.71, pmix4 -0.16, pmix6 +0.77 vs the -0.74 filler floor), dropping break-even 4/12 -> 2/12.
GATES, in `runs/think32_abstain/config.sh` verbatim: **D1 @300 is a DIAGNOSTIC WITH NO KILL** (an
abstaining writer must learn WHERE to speak; the clause exists so no future tick invents a gate there),
G1 @600 own(1-11) >= 0.0722 (run 31 @600, same register same step: do no harm), G2 @1000 >= 0.105
(run 31's G2 verbatim so both runs share ONE ladder), G3 @1500 >= 0.154 (own@0 0.31 + 11*0.154 = 2.0/12
= pmix2 = break-even; if it clears, the PAIRED thinkmode own-vs-pause probe becomes the headline).
REGISTERED FAILURE MODE, before any data: the cheapest policy under this mask is all-filler, which is
run 26, scores -0.74 and buys nothing. own(1-11) -> 0 so the gates exclude it, but if it lands near zero
the write-up says "collapsed to silence", not "failed to learn".
Init = run 31 @800, NOT run 25 @1500: run 31 bought own@0 0.047 -> 0.312 and is flat, so re-buying those
800 steps costs ~300 steps for nothing. **Stated caveat: run 32 does not share an init with runs 27-31,
so matched-step comparisons to them are LEVEL comparisons only** -- acceptable because the instrument is
absolute (agreement vs true held-out text), not reader-relative.

The 06:07 tick (me) justified `--abstain-mode freq` with the abstention ladder's `pmix6 +0.77` vs the

ladder implied +0.5 to +2. Cause, read out of the code: `probe_oracle_offset.py`'s pmix<K> blanks
positions with `rng.choice(LEN, LEN-PK)` -- **uniformly at random**, so its survivors include content
words -- while the freq mask keeps a true token only where it is a **top-300 unigram**, i.e. precisely
the tokens the reader can already predict. Same count, systematically less informative subset. The rung
run 32 actually trains on had never been measured.

do NOT kill it on orG.** Frequency selection costs ~0 at m=4 (almost every token is frequent anyway)

**(2) THE CLAUSE THAT PASSED IS THE MORE IMPORTANT NUMBER AND IT REPLICATES RUN 56.** With `--imit-w 0` -- the
  writer is never shown what to write, ever -- the greedy thought opens with the CORRECT looked-up value on 94% of
  1-hop anchors, and the content survives depth: `pvls_greedy` 0.938 / 0.854 / 0.818 / 0.715 / **0.617** at hops
  1 / 2 / 3-4 / 5-7 / 8-10. Run 56 read 0.98 at step 200 (n=54) under a different sampler. **Two runs, two
  samplers: the discovery of thought CONTENT from the answer reward alone is real.** Every run before 56 in this
  family emitted no answer-vocabulary tokens at all. Everything from here is built to protect this.

**(3) DEFECT 1 (new gotcha G72): THE STOP FLOOR TRUNCATES THE ANSWER -- AND IT IS OUR SETTING, NOT THE POLICY.**
  `--stop-explore 0.1` worked: greedy length **22.1 @500 -> 2.0 @850**, then flat. It is flat because it is on the
  FLOOR. `--min-think N` makes `</T>` legal at slot position `t >= N` (`think_par.py:285`), i.e. N counts TOKENS;
  a chase value is TWO digit tokens (`synth.py:_two`, l.102-129); and this writer has learned to OPEN WITH A SPACE
  (dumps at steps 800-850: `' 4 </T>'`, `' 9 </T>'`, gains +1.53/-0.76/+0.98 -- the space-tolerant `pvls_*` counter
  added at 17:07 exists only because of that habit). So under `--min-think 2` the shortest legal thought is
  **SPACE + ONE DIGIT**, half an answer, and a reward that prefers short thoughts drives the policy onto it.
  It knows the value (0.938) and truncates it (EM 0.365). Companion to G39 (the price is superlinear in length).

**(4) DEFECT 2 (new gotcha G73): THE 1-HOP-ONLY CURRICULUM PHASE INSTALLED "THE ANSWER IS THE FIRST VALUE".**
  `--synth-hops 1 --synth-hops-max 10 --synth-hops-ramp 250` draws hops `U{1..min(10, 1+step//250)}`
  (`think_train.py:589-593`), so the model saw ONLY 1-hop problems for 250 steps -- and at one hop the first value
  of the chain IS the answer. Look at the **`tf` column** above, not at greedy: teacher-forcing hands the model the
  TRUE chain `v1 v2` and asks for `v2`, and it scores **0.021 at 2 hops** against 0.958 at 1 hop, after a further
  250 steps of 2-hop training. **A reader that cannot cash a chain it is GIVEN makes the reward
  `p(answer|thought) - p(answer|clean)` content-free** -- the run-52 lesson arriving by a new road. For scale, at
  the SAME step from the SAME init, run 55 (hops `U{3..10}` from step 0) read `tf` **0.846** at hops 3-4 and 0.403
  DEEP. An easy rung is for EXPLORATION: keep it as a FRACTION of a mixture, never as a PHASE.

**(5) A READING I CHECKED AND WOULD NOT LET MYSELF MAKE.** "Run 57's clean EM at hops 3-4 is 0.039 against run
  55's 0.504, so the curriculum DESTROYED multi-hop ability" -- no. Run 57 had never been trained on a 3-hop
  problem at step 500, so a low `clean` there is expected and proves nothing. The claim that survives is the
  narrow one in (4): **2 hops, teacher-forced, after 250 steps of 2-hop training, 0.021.** That is the number G73
  rests on.

### 22:40 addendum to the 22:07 tick -- a risk in my own fix, recorded before any run-58 data
`--min-think 3` makes the CANONICAL 1-hop thought illegal: the demonstration scratchpad for one hop is exactly two
digit tokens (`synth.py`, `S` gets no leading space at `i=0`) and the floor is now three. I set it at three anyway,
for two reasons: run 57's writer independently learned to open with a SPACE, so its own 1-hop form is SPACE + two
digits = exactly 3; and the alternative, 2, is MEASURED to truncate (G72). **So the failure mode to look for at
check A is the OPPOSITE of run 57's: a 1-hop greedy thought of THREE DIGITS -- the value plus one junk digit.**
Diagnostic, stated now so the 05:40 read is not improvised: 1-hop `pvls_greedy` still >= 0.9 while `EM(greedy)` <
`EM(clean)`, with `len_g` ~3 and no leading space in the probe's `examples`. If A fails that way the floor is not
the fix, and the next run keeps `--min-think 2` and pays for length some other way. Only 1-hop problems are
affected; at two hops the demonstration is already five tokens. Recorded as a comment at the end of
`runs/think58_mixed/config.sh` (comment only -- the FLAGS array is untouched and was sourced at launch).

**(3) G73's RULE IS FALSIFIED BY RUN 58; ITS OBSERVATION STANDS (new gotcha G75).** G73 told run 58 to keep the
  hard rung from step 0 (`--synth-hops-ramp 0`). Run 58 did exactly that and the discovery died: 1-hop
  `pvls_greedy` **0.938 (run 57) -> 0.271 (run 58)**, same step, same probe, same init. The "dozens of easy anchors
  per step is enough" argument counts ANCHORS, not REWARD: on the other 90% nothing pays for "emit the looked-up
  value", so the behaviour is swamped before it is found. The two symptoms are one -- with nothing discovered no
  short thought earns anything either, so `--stop-explore` has nothing to pull toward and the greedy row sits at
  the cap (32.0 vs run 57's 22.2 and falling at the same step). **Size an exploration rung by the fraction of the
  REWARD it carries, not by the count of anchors it occupies.**

the data. `h ~ U{hops..hops_max}` means **1-hop and 2-hop have identical share trajectories at every step**
(both 33% @500, both 20% @1000), yet 1-hop `EM(clean)` FELL 0.729 -> 0.438 while 2-hop ROSE 0.146 -> 0.542.
Share explains the EM movements (each band converges to what its CURRENT share supports; the 100%-1-hop phase
of steps 0-249 over-trained 1-hop and it regressed). **Share cannot explain the writer: the deep bands gained
share from zero and their `pvls_greedy` collapsed anyway** (>=8: 0.365 -> 0.104 -> 0.035).

HANDED the true chain, which upper-bounds what ANY writer could earn -- is **zero or negative at every depth >= 3,

strength. That is the mechanism for "perfect format, rotting content": `--min-think 3` pins the form (`len_g`
exactly 3 on **432/432**) while the content takes a full-strength random walk, and by @1100 the note is a net

 (b) **Run 59's own log rejects normality by a mile.** `n_anch` = 4 per step (median; max 9). Simulating the null
   at that anchor count: mean 1.576, sd **0.173**, P(per-step ratio < 1.0) = **0 of 200,000**. Observed run 59:

    rescues 1 of 76 and **BREAKS 18 of the 116** it could already answer. **Costs 18, buys 1. Pure damage.**
  - **2 hops (the leading value is an intermediate it does NOT have):** on problems it cannot answer it writes
    the correct **first step 77/133 = 58%** and converts only **9/133 = 6.8%**. It knows step one and never

**(a) I was WRONG that the collapse to a 2-token note was pure damage.** That note CLEARS THE FILLER BAR at
4.4 s.e. The shortening was ADAPTATION, not surrender: a one-number note is cheap enough to be affordable and
still carries something. My 04:07 framing ("it was learning to say nothing") overstated it -- it learned to say

0.88, so its note is more consistent; that is not a result.) Run 63 did not fail by damaging the model at o=-7,

through. So *there is no single "untrained bar"*: every gate must be read against **the init at that gate's own
offset**, and any comparison of a run to its own earlier self across an offset change is confounded. The o=-15
figure had been quoted in `SUPERVISOR.md` sec. 00S as if it were THE bar; it is one point on a steep curve.

**(3) THE NEW FINDING, and it reframes runs 60-64 (G91).** `span - filler` is the reader's sensitivity to a
PERFECT note -- a quantity **the writer cannot influence at all** -- and it falls by a third in 400 steps
(+15.65 -> +9.01). So the "the writer writes worse notes" frame that drove five successive successor choices is
at least partly wrong: **the reader is going deaf to the slot itself.** `own/span` also falls (0.45 -> 0.23), so
the writer is losing ground too; both are real and only the pair separates them. Rule added: always report
`span - filler` beside `own - filler`, and quote the margin as a fraction of `clean` as well as in nats (because

So the drop is not REINFORCE; it is **one-off adaptation shock** -- the cost of converting a vanilla next-token
model to the block-insertion format under warmup -- and shock and erosion have OPPOSITE successors (shock ->
change the starting point; erosion -> change the objective term that is on while the margin falls). A level read
at step 200 cannot tell them apart. This generalises G91 ("probe the trend before arguing about a level"): **the
trend needs its FIRST point, not just two late ones.** `--rl-w 0.25` is now REMOVED from the sec. 00S queue.

still being trained away, and the ceiling is drifting down with it. What is new is that in run 64 that measure
and `own/span` fell TOGETHER (which is what made "the reader is going deaf" look like the whole story), and in
run 65 they have **decoupled**: `own/span` rises through a falling `span-filler/clean`. So reader deafness is
real, is still running, and does NOT by itself determine whether the writer is learning. Steer on `own/span`

**(1) THE ARMED PROBES DELIVERED THE WHOLE UNTRAINED SLIDE, and it contradicts the intuition five runs were
steered by.** `agent/init_refs.sh` finished (o=-13/-11/-9), so with the three already on disk the init is now
measured at every offset run 65 visits -- G88 discharged for this run. The task does not get harder because an
oracle note gets weaker. **It gets stronger.** What collapses is the untrained model's ability to produce one:
```
   offset      own-filler        span-filler   own/span   of/clean
   init -15    +6.93 +- 0.85       +15.65       0.449      39.4%
   init -13    +5.48 +- 0.86       +17.07       0.323      30.2%
   init -11    +4.85 +- 1.03       +17.97       0.264      26.3%
   init  -9    +1.71 +- 0.91       +18.08       0.108       9.4%

   r65 @800 -11  +2.28 +- 0.53     +11.95       0.331      75.0% (sf/clean)
```
Two consequences. (a) The init's bar gets CHEAP from o=-9 on, exactly where the science gets hard -- so "beats
the init" must always be quoted with `own/span`, or a late pass gets oversold. (b) Restate a nat bar in oracle
share before trusting it: G2's +3.54 at o=-7 is only `own/span` ~= **0.185**.

**(2) G93, FOUND BEFORE THE CHECKPOINT EXISTED: run 65's G2 clause names the wrong stage.** `--span-sched`
switches **at** the listed step, so step 1000 has trained 200 steps at o=-9 and ZERO at o=-7. Run 65's config
used that fact CORRECTLY for G1b ("the step-400 checkpoint is still an o=-15 model") and then, forty lines
later, inverted it for G2 ("o=-7, the schedule's offset at step 1000"). Same sitting, same tick, both clauses.
G2 is therefore a TRANSFER test and harsher than it reads. **I did not move it.** At step 746, before
step_0001000.pt could exist, I appended a dated amendment to `runs/think65_nofiller/config.sh` that (a) pins
G2's arithmetic to ONE number so no later tick can argue it -- 2 s.e. **of the difference**, which is how run 63
was judged at this offset, giving **+3.54** (init +1.41 +- 0.88, probe s.e. ~0.60) -- and (b) pre-registers how
a FAIL resolves: **a G2 fail alone does not stop the run**; it must also fail step 1000 @ o=-9 (bar **+3.90**,
init +1.71 +- 0.91, the TRAINED-offset test) AND step 1200 @ o=-7 (bar **+3.54**, the fair same-offset test).
Both were already armed by the 08:07 tick, so this costs nothing and removes all judgement from the next tick.

**(3) I RECORDED A FORECAST AT 10:07 AND IT WAS FALSIFIED AT 10:33, IN THIS TICK. Writing it down is the point.**
The amendment's clause (c) predicted G2 would PASS WITH ROOM, because own/span 0.468 was 2.5x its 0.185
bar-equivalent and the run "would have to shed 60% of its oracle share to fail". Then the armed step-800 probe
landed: **own-filler +2.28 +- 0.53 at o=-11, down -2.10 +- 0.80 from step 600; own/span 0.468 -> 0.331.** Run 65
is now **2.57 +- 1.16 (2.2 s.e.) BELOW the init** at o=-11 in nats, though still above it in oracle share (0.331
vs 0.264). Extrapolating the per-stage relative loss (-29%, where the init loses 18% over the same crossing)
gives ~0.235 at o=-9 and ~0.167 at o=-7 against the 0.185 bar: **G2 is borderline-to-failing, not comfortable.**
What I got wrong, stated plainly: I treated `own/span` as a writer property that CARRIES across stages. It does
not -- **it is re-earned at every offset.** Recorded in config.sh, SUPERVISOR.md sec. 00S and POSTMORTEM G93 as a
correction appended beside the original claim, not an edit over it.

**(4) THE DECOMPOSITION IS THE USEFUL PART, AND IT POINTS THE OPPOSITE WAY FROM RUN 64.** Across this stage
`span-filler / clean` was **FLAT** (72.9% -> 75.0%) while `own/span` fell. So the reader did NOT go deafer: the
**WRITER** lost ground as the span slid. Run 64 failed with both falling together and its successor was a reader
lever (`--pause-frac 0`, which worked). This is the CURRICULUM branch of sec. 00S item 2 instead. The amendment's
EXCEPTION clause -- "if own/span held while the nats failed, it is the reader" -- is therefore NOT triggered.

**(5) THE SHAPE OF THE DECAY NAMES A DIFFERENT LEVER THAN THE ONE REGISTERED, and I deliberately did not act on
it.** The loss is not spread over training time; it is paid **at** the stage change and it GROWS with the jump:
o=-15 -> -13 cost ~0 (+4.44 -> +4.39), o=-13 -> -11 cost -2.10. The span is x[n+o..n+o+14], so those crossings
take the number of FUTURE tokens inside it 0 -> 2 -> 4. If the cost tracks the JUMP rather than the elapsed
steps, the lever is the slide's **step size (+1 per stage)**, not its **time per stage (+2 every 400 steps)**,
which is what item 2 registers. A run spent on the wrong one of those is ~9 hours. Registered as a question for
the tick that has the step-1000/1200 numbers, with an instruction to say which of the two the data supports --
not as a pre-emption of the registered successor.

already existed A was true and the echo ran anyway -- 26 spurious "archived step_0000500.pt" lines over 70
minutes. The `ln` itself was correctly skipped, so no data was at risk, but the log invited the next tick to
chase archive churn that was not happening (I spent part of this tick doing exactly that: `grep -rln` missed it

Backup `archive_ckpts.sh.bak_pre_precedence_20260930_1007`. **A `||`-guard followed by `&&` is not a guard.**

**(2) WHY, AND IT IS EXACT ARITHMETIC.** `REW = G - len_cost*S0`; `--baseline loo` gives
`ADV_R[r] = REW[r] - mean_{j!=r} REW[j]`. **Any term with the same value for every rollout of an anchor
subtracts out exactly.** While every rollout is at `len 15` -- run 65 held that until **step 514** --
`len_cost*S0` is exactly such a term (verified numerically, max |ADV difference| 8.9e-16). `--len-cost`
appears nowhere else bar the unused `--baseline greedy` branch. So run 66's one flag is identically
inert for 513 steps. **The 12:07 tick verified that the FLAGS array differed in exactly one line; it did
not verify that the line could move a gradient.** That is the check that was missing and it is now
00S.0 item 7(g).

run 65 right up to the step the length price first acts, differing only from there, with no confound
from seed, data order or warmup. H1 and R3 stand.

Item 7(c) proposed scoring the reward against a FILLER slot instead of silence, arguing the block price
swamps the between-rollout content differences. `_score()` returns `lw(c) - _base` and `_base` is the
SAME vector for every rollout, so it cancels in `ADV_R` exactly (max |ADV difference| 1.8e-15 between a
silence and a filler baseline). The absolute gain level reaches the gradient nowhere else: `elig`
(l.935) is logging only, never a loss weight. **The block price was never in the reward. "The reward is
own-vs-silence" (G52) describes the METRIC `g`, not the objective -- the objective has always been a
pure between-rollout content comparison.** 7(c) is struck in SUPERVISOR.md. Recorded as G96(a).
Both retired hypotheses -- the length price and the reward baseline -- were arguments about the
ABSOLUTE level of the reward, and the objective only ever sees DIFFERENCES between rollouts of one
anchor. That is one mistake made twice in one day, and it is now a standing pre-launch check.

**(5) WHAT THE ALGEBRA DID FIND, AND IT FITS RUN 65'S ENDING BETTER THAN THE LENGTH PRICE DOES (G96).**
One line on from the cancellation (l.989-992):
```
  mu = mean(adv_paired); sig = sd(adv_paired)
  A  = clip((adv_paired - mu) / (sig + 1e-6), +-reward_clip) * rlf      # reward_clip is 7.1 here
```
The advantage is z-scored with **no floor**, so it is **scale-invariant**. At this lineage's actual
`--reward-clip 7.1` the clip essentially never binds, so `mean|A|` is pinned at `sqrt(2/pi) = 0.798`
for ANY spread:
```
   adv sd 2.180 -> mean|A| 0.790 (0% clipped)      adv sd 0.060 -> mean|A| 0.800 (0% clipped)
   adv sd 0.500 -> mean|A| 0.770 (0% clipped)      adv sd 0.006 -> mean|A| 0.812 (0% clipped)
```
**The trainer is by construction incapable of noticing that its reward has gone silent.** It
renormalises what is left -- at `g_sd 0.06`, numerical noise -- to full scale and keeps applying it at
`rl_w 0.5`. This needs no length price, which is why it is a successor to run 66 and not a variant.
**The evidence is already on disk and it is the fact I could not fit into the length story this
morning:** a dead gradient leaves the policy FROZEN, but run 65's policy was moving hard at `g_sd 0.06`
-- converging onto `of   </T` at 553 of ~840 prefixes, reg% 50.7. A frozen reward with a fast-moving
policy is the signature of full-scale updates on noise, and nothing else in the objective explains it
(`--imit-w` is 0; `p_or` is constant at its floor for steps 800-1200 while the collapse deepens).

**(6) BUILT AND TESTED: `--adv-sig-floor`, default 0.0.** Divisor becomes `max(sig, floor)`. At floor 0
the expression is **bit-identical** to the old one (`sig` is a sqrt, so `max(sig,0.0) == sig`; measured
max |A difference| **0.0e+00** over run 65's whole `g_sd` trajectory), so a crash-relaunch of run 66 off
the edited file is safe. At floor 0.5 the healthy phase is untouched and the RL term fades exactly over
the collapse window: `g_sd 1.08 -> 0.828 both ways`; `g_sd 0.33 -> 0.768 vs 0.472`; `g_sd 0.06 ->
0.782 vs 0.103`. `py_compile` OK; `USE_TORCH_XLA=0 python test_rollouts.py` green in full, before and
after. **I also had to add instrumentation, because `sig` was observable nowhere**: `adv_sig` and
`adv_absA` now go to `metrics.jsonl`, without which a floor run could not be distinguished from a
no-floor run. Run 66 was launched before that patch, so its metrics will lack the keys -- reconstruct
from `g_sd * 1.155` and say so.

that do not survive the baseline subtraction; this is a GATE that was never in the objective at all.

**(3) THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MORE, AND IT IS AGAINST MY OWN RULER.** Writing (2) up meant pulling the
absolute arms out of `armed.log`, and they do not say what the margin says (`shuf := own - own_minus_shuf`):
```
 rung    own r67  own r68 | shuf r67 shuf r68 | span r67 span r68 | clean r67 clean r68
  600    +7.37   +10.10   |  +3.81    +7.96   |  +16.08   +15.89  |  +18.52    +18.48
  800    +6.53   +13.86   |  +2.97   +11.48   |  +16.20   +20.77  |  +17.54    +21.66
 1000    +2.73   +15.28   |  -0.25   +13.70   |  +14.46   +24.08  |  +13.76    +22.83
 1800    -0.37     (n/a)  |  -2.38     (n/a)  |  +16.52     (n/a) |   +7.69      (n/a)
```
**At rung 600 the two runs are the same run on every absolute** (own within 2.7, span and clean within
0.2). **By rung 1000 they are not.** Run 67's own-note gain goes +7.37 -> +2.73 -> **-0.37**; its no-note
ceiling `clean` goes +18.52 -> **+7.69**. Run 68's go the other way (+15.28, +22.83).
**And run 67's margin is built from the control going NEGATIVE.** At 1000 the margin **+2.98** exceeds
the entire value of the note (**+2.73**) because the shuffled arm is **-0.25**. At 1800 the margin is
**+2.01 while the own note is worth -0.37** -- the note makes the model *worse than no note*, and the
gated quantity reports that as a healthy margin. Run 68, writer-gradient-free, has the *smaller* margin
(+1.58) with **both** arms large (+15.28/+13.70).
**So `--xanchor-w 1.0` with `--rl-w 0.5` is not learning to write a better note. It is learning to stop
using notes, and the own-note arm decays slowest.** A margin can be won by lifting the numerator or by
wrecking the denominator; this one was the second. **Same family as G94's broken ruler, and this time it
is in the quantity every run since 60 has gated on.** It does **not** overturn (1) -- that is a matched
contrast, the sign stands -- it changes *what the sign protects*: the RL term slows the decay of the
own-note arm **in a regime where both arms and the whole reader are decaying.** Not "makes the note good".
**NEW STANDING RULE, and it is cheap because the daemons already log both numbers: no `own_minus_shuf`
verdict is ever stated again without `own` and `shuf` printed beside it.**

## 2026-10-03 22:07 (headless tick) -- THE MONITOR WAS ~3 MINUTES FROM STOPPING A HEALTHY RUN 86 ON A CLAUSE THAT COMPARES TWO RATES COMPUTED UNDER DIFFERENT RULES. CAUGHT, FIXED, TESTED SIX WAYS, RE-ARMED; THE SAME FLAW WAS IN THE PROBE THE RESULT IS READ FROM (G127)

**(1) THE NEAR MISS, AND IT WAS ARITHMETIC, NOT A PROBLEM WITH THE RUN.** `status.py` printed run 86 at step 485-522
with `ctrl 7%` against `keep 2%`, which satisfies the monitor's **D4 second clause** (`rolling-300 ctrl_rate >=
keep_rate`, armed after step 500). Measured: rolling-300 `keep_rate` **0.0263**, `ctrl_rate` **0.0711**. The monitor
had last ticked 22:01:18 on a 600 s loop, so the next evaluation was due **22:11:18** and the clock read 22:08 --
it would have stopped the run and spent one of the three remaining ladder launches. **Cause:
`think_entropy.py:540` vs `:555` -- `keep_rate` comes from `decide_contrast()` (beat silence by `margin` AND beat
its own shuffle by `cmargin`, TWO conditions) while `ctrl_rate` comes from plain `decide()` on the shuffled thought
(`margin` only, ONE condition). A strictly harder rule passes less often, so on any `--contrast-margin` run
`ctrl_rate >= keep_rate` holds BY CONSTRUCTION.** The proof it is structural rather than a degradation: it is true
in **every 100-step bin from step 0** -- bin 0 keep **0.0294** vs ctrl **0.0634**, before training could do
anything -- with `n_ctrl` ~**101,800 per bin** (contrast runs force the shuffled pass every micro, not every 4th),
so it is not noise. **Killed the monitor by its process group** `kill -- -246231` at 22:08, confirmed 0 monitors and
0 orphaned `sleep` left in that pgid, and confirmed the run itself was untouched (66 workers, `metrics.jsonl` still
growing, step 537 -> 538 across the kill).

**(2) WHY IT HAD NOT BITTEN BEFORE, WHICH IS THE PART THAT GENERALISES.** Runs 85 and 86 introduced a new keep rule
interactively and inherited run 83's monitor unexamined. **D4 arms at step 500 and run 85 was stopped at step ~230**
-- run 86 is simply the first contrast run to live long enough to be falsely derailed. A clause that is wrong by
construction can sit latent across several runs and then fire on the first healthy one. This is **G84's rule** --
before launch, walk every derail clause and ask what it reads on a HEALTHY run of THIS design, and write the dead
ones down -- for at least the sixth time (after G54/G56(c)/G76/G77/G84), and the first time it nearly cost a run.

**(3) FIXED NARROWLY AND TESTED BEFORE ARMING, WHICH IS THE LESSON THE 20:07 TICK PAID FOR.** `derail_check` now
extracts the run's own `--contrast-margin` (same one-liner as the probe call at l.153) and passes it to the python;

are byte-identical. Extracted the patched 42-line checker to `/tmp/derail_test.py` and ran **six** cases:

**(5) THE SAME FLAW IS IN `probe_entropy.py`, WHICH IS WHERE THE RESULT IS READ FROM, SO `rungs.tsv`'s CONTROL IS
NOT LIKE-FOR-LIKE EITHER.** Line 114 computes `ctrl_keep_rate` with plain `decide()` on the shuffle even when

**(6) RUN 86 DID NOT COLLAPSE THE WAY 83/84/85 DID. IT COLLAPSED ON AN AXIS NONE OF THE INSTRUMENTS WATCH: LENGTH.**
50-step bins: `len_gen` **64.0 for 250 steps, then 64 -> 6.5 between steps 250 and 450, then FLAT at ~6** (6.52 /
5.90 / 6.16 over bins 450/500/550). Every token-level collapse instrument reads clean -- `digit_share` **0.02**,
`rep_kept` **0.18** (bar 0.5), `open_share` **0.09**. Alongside: `keep_rate` 0.037 -> **0.020**, `imit_ce` 2.71 ->
**0.94** (falling = the writer converging onto its kept set), `drop_full` -0.72 -> **-3.20**. Base intact: `ntp1`
2.77-2.83 on the vanilla blocks, gnorm 0.48, 0 NaN, 66 workers. **A mechanism that predicts the plateau:** kept
length is capped at the thought's own generated length and a thought passing at the first check is kept at
<= 8 tokens, so imitation teaches short thoughts and the writer shortens -- but **the contrast rule puts its own
floor under this**, because `rng.permutation` of 1 token is the identity (`ls - l` exactly 0 < 1.0, so a 1-token

**(1) FIRST ACTION WAS THE ONE THE PROMPT ASKED FOR -- "CHECK WHETHER THE DEVICE IS IDLE" -- AND IT IS NOT.** A

**(2) WHY THIS TICK EXISTS: `ticks.log` 08:07 reads `tick end rc=0 (2743 bytes)` -- THE 08:07 TICK SUCCEEDED.** It
stopped run 87 and launched run 88. Then the auth detector it had just built matched **its own summary**, which
quoted the OAuth error string it had spent the tick fixing. Flag dropped, loud line written, retry fired: me. **A
detector that reads the tick's prose for a machine signal gets more likely to misfire the better the tick writes
up its work**, because a tick's output is a report about exactly the conditions the detector watches for. Worse,
the twin check on the retry's log would have read **this** entry's summary -- also about authentication -- declared
`*** RETRY ALSO FAILED ***` and `OWNER ACTION NEEDED`, and left the flag set for 10:07. Both halves of the 08:07
fix failed closed on a healthy supervisor. That is **G128**, four items, now at the top of `agent/SUPERVISOR.md`
(backup `agent/SUPERVISOR.md.bak_pre_g128_20261004_0825`).

**(3) THE REPLACEMENT JUDGES A TICK BY `rc` AND OUTPUT SIZE, BOTH PRODUCED BY THE KERNEL AND THE SHELL, NEVER BY
THE MODEL -- AND IT IS STRICTLY BROADER THAN WHAT IT REPLACES.** `DEAD=1` iff `rc != 0` **or** `bytes < 400`
(real ticks: 2.3-3.6 KB; the three dead ones: 73 bytes), and the retry is judged by the same two numbers rather
than by grepping its write-up. This now also catches crashes, OOM kills, a `timeout` kill and empty-but-rc-0
output, none of which the string grep could see. The loud line became `*** TICK PRODUCED NO WORK ***` and carries
`rc`, `bytes` and `elapsed`. **Tested six ways against a stub `claude` before arming**: healthy -> nothing;
**healthy log whose prose quotes the OAuth error -> nothing** (the bug above, now the regression test); auth-fail
then good -> loud line + flag + retry + flag cleared; auth-fail twice -> loud line, flag KEPT, owner-action line;
`rc=0` with 0 bytes -> caught as dead; slow death -> no retry, flag left. Backup
`agent/tick.sh.bak_pre_selfref_20261004_0825`.

**(4) A NEW HOLE FOUND WHILE WRITING IT, AND CLOSED: A RETRY MUST FIT IN THE GAP BEFORE THE NEXT CRON TICK.** The
08:07 version would retry **any** auth-matching tick, including one killed at its `timeout 5400`. That retry would
still be running when the next 2-hourly tick fires, and that tick hits `flock -n 9 || exit 0` at line 6 -- **which
exits without logging anything at all**, recreating the exact silence G127 was written about, this time caused by
the fix for it. The retry is now gated on `elapsed < 600`; a slow death gets the loud line and the flag and the
next tick decides. (The unlogged `flock` skip is a remaining gap, named in G128 item 3: missing ticks with no
"skip" line = suspect an overrunning predecessor.)

Discharging obligation 2 in `agent/scratchpad/price_run95_baseline.py` broke the design's own argument.
`DESIGN_run95_baseline.md` claimed the group-mean baseline reinforces every thought with `mu < r < 0` and
"that band is the volume". True of the advantage, FALSE of the gradient: `--topk 2` sits between them
(`think_grpo_gate.py:473`). Under `--abstain-free` silence scores `r = 0` exactly and all rows in a spot
share `mu` and `sd`, so ordering by `A` IS ordering by `r`; **every silence row outranks every harmful
thought**, and a harmful thought reaches the top-K only if its group of 6 holds fewer than 2 silence rows
-- `(1-p)^6 + 6p(1-p)^5` = **3.5% of spots at p=0.613**, exact, no simulation. A gate at 1.40x its help
rate is not driven by 3.5% of spots. **The replacement follows the evidence instead: top-K rewards the gate
wherever the BEST OF SIX thoughts beats silence, and deployment samples ONE -- which predicts bar (b)
passing, bar (a) failing at every rung, and the volume, all at once.** New flag `--gate-adv mean` (the gate
DECISION token at line 254 carries the group's mean speaking advantage; content positions keep their own),
so break-even becomes bar (a) by construction. Written up as `DESIGN_run95_baseline.md` R1-R5 (+68 lines,
backup `.bak_pre_revision_20261005_2007`). **NOT IMPLEMENTED, no trainer file touched**, obligations 1, 3,
4 and the filler row of 2 still owed, and obligation 4's metric redefined to `best_pos - mean_pos` because
the original `leak` metric would have measured the 3.5% channel.

device logs +0.0735 on the same steps. `A_ab` is divided by `M["n_ab"]`, which accumulates `v.sum()` -- the
valid-SPOT count, not the abstain-ROW count -- so it looked like a ~3.7x normalisation error that would
have made B309/B326/B335 artefacts of the abstention rate. I checked before writing: numerator and
denominator carry the same weight, `n_ab/n_valid` is exactly 256.000 on every 40-step block of both runs,
and the corrected series is below run 93's on 20/20 blocks just as the logged one is. **The model was the
suspect, not the device. G144 ITEM 5.**

  **INIT** -- `think_bestof.py:159-162` creates both heads zero-weight with **bias -0.8**, so an untrained head emits
  `p0 = sigmoid(-0.8) = 0.3100` at every anchor; its BCE is `-(y ln p0 + (1-y) ln(1-p0))` with the block's mean label.
  **FLOOR** -- cross-entropy is LINEAR in the soft label, so the best constant predictor is the mean label itself and
  its BCE is exactly `H(mean label)`. Above the floor = the base rate is not learned; below = real information.
  Labels: `gate_pre` <- `helps_share` (mean = `helps`); `gate_post` <- `gain>0` on 2 rows/spot (mean = `(best_helps+helps)/2`).

**ITEM 1 -- I PUBLISHED A STEADY STEP COST OFF A STEP THAT RAN AT HALF THE BATCH, AND THE CONVERSION FACTOR WAS
ALREADY IN THE FILE I WAS QUOTING FROM.** The 20:45 verdict read launch 5's smoke step 2 (13.98 s) as the steady
cost and built the whole handoff on it. **OLD: 14.0 s/step, "TWICE AS FAST as launch 1", 45 h total, step
5000-5500 by 22:07, rung 1 at ~21:29. NEW: 25.24 s/step median (steps 101-156, both ends pinned), 17% faster
than launch 1's 30.35 s, 80.8 h total, step 156 at 22:07, rung 1 at 22:21.** The prediction was out by a factor
of ~32 in step count. **MECHANISM: `run_think.sh:80` runs the smoke with `--grad-accum 2`; training runs
`--grad-accum 4`.** The smoke's step 2 is a half-batch step. Launch 1's own smoke step 2 was 15.48 s against its
steady 30.35 s -- **a 1.96x factor sitting on disk in the same file** -- and applying it to launch 5's 13.98 s
predicts 27.4 s against the observed 25.2 s (8% error). `config.sh`'s own 17:19 note even spells the conversion
out: "step 2: 15.5 s at GA 2 -> ~31 s/step at GA 4". I had the right arithmetic in front of me and did not use it.
BINDING: last tick's lesson ("never register a throughput band off step 0 or step 1") was too narrow and is
replaced by: **a throughput number is quoted only from steps of the TRAINING process at the run's own GA; the
smoke is a different batch size and is never a source for a steady cost.** Launch 5 was never at 14 s -- even
steps 3-20 ran 26.2 s.

**ITEM 2 -- B648 FAILS OUT-OF-SAMPLE. THE r_std EARLY WARNING HAS CRIED WOLF SIX TIMES AND THE RUN IS 79 STEPS
PAST THE CLIFF IT WAS BUILT TO PREDICT.** Scored with each run's OWN scale-free threshold (median(r_std,10-49)
x 1.25), which is how the clause is defined:
  - launch 1 (thr 2.834): crossings **[96, 97, 98, 99]** only. **ZERO false positives in 96 healthy steps -- the
    in-sample claim in `collapse_watch.py` is CORRECT.** (My first pass applied launch 5's threshold to launch 1
    and wrongly made it 8 false positives; corrected here before use.)
  - launch 5 (thr 2.665): crossings **[79, 105, 129, 130, 131, 157]**, max r_std 3.092, **no collapse**, and the
    collapse clause has never fired. Launch 1's cliff was step 97->98; launch 5 is at 177.
**MECHANISM, and it is a design flaw not bad luck: the baseline window (steps 10-49) lies inside LR warmup
(`--warmup-steps 100`).** Launch 5's r_std median goes 2.132 (baseline) -> 2.445 (steps 100-156), i.e. **+14.7%
of ordinary post-warmup drift against a multiplier of only +25% -- the drift eats 59% of the margin before any
collapse risk is involved.** Launch 1 never showed this because it died at step 98, right as warmup ended.
B648 is now SCORED and CLOSED. **I am deliberately NOT retuning the threshold**: the only separable positive is
launch 1's step 97 (r_std 8.385), which is simultaneous with gain_mean -13.76, so it is detection, not
prediction, and refitting on one positive example is how this project has misled itself before.
**What DOES work is already armed and needs no change:** the collapse clause (best_helps == 0 or gain_best < -5
for 3 consecutive steps) fires at launch 1's step 100, two steps after the cliff, with no false positives.
**And the registered D2 clause is the slow one: launch 1's open_share was still 0.127 at step 98 with
gain_mean -67.73, and only crossed 0.80 at step 120 -- D2 lags the actual collapse by 22 steps.** (`collapse_watch.py`'s
header says 12; the file record should read **22**.) So D2 is not the collapse guard for this trainer; the

So the max of the sample is improving while the population of thoughts is not: the pre-registered failure

which has very little power, so "flat" here means "no detectable trend", not "proven flat".** Note also
`r_std` rose 2.11 -> 2.50 across the windows: gain_best up + gain_mean flat + spread up is the upper tail
widening, which is not the same as pure static selection (pure selection with a fixed distribution would hold

decided, and B658 registers it BEFORE the data.

  at deployable volumes, and is **NEGATIVE at speak 0.50** (-0.41/-1.39/-1.38) -- more than half the triggered
  anchors are positions where the best available single thought hurts.
**This is the clearest negative the programme has produced, and it is not about capacity or tuning: the
information needed to tell a good thought from a bad one is not present in the model's state at the point
where it would have to decide.** Two independent channels agree -- six hand-built label-free gates and a
trained head, in-training and at the probe.

  **-0.0096 = 1.38%**; accuracy 0.5507 against a majority-class 0.5291, i.e. **+0.022**.

**ITEM 2 -- ONE THING *IS* SHUT, PERMANENTLY, AND IT NEEDS NO MODEL AT ALL.** Precision at speak rate `q` can
never exceed `pi/q`. So a gate can break even only if `bar*q <= pi`, i.e.
**`q <= q_max = pi/bar`**. At rung 4 that is **0.1562/0.7637 = 0.2045**. At rungs 1-3: 0.275 / 0.211 / 0.211.
**No gate, at any AUC, with any amount of training, can break even while speaking at more than ~one position
in five** -- and `q_max` is **falling**, because `pi` is falling (item 3). This is why the q=0.23 and q=0.50
columns in `decision_*.txt` have never had a positive cell and never will: `auc_bar_0407.py` prints
**"IMPOSSIBLE at any AUC"** for both. The whole programme has been reading those columns as evidence about the
ranker when they were arithmetically dead before the ranker was consulted. **Registered as a standing rule
(binding 1 below).**

**0.105**, so `--rl-w` needs no change.

`np.mean([])`/`np.std([], ddof=1)` give NaN, `json.dump` writes them, the script **exits 0**, and
`ceiling_rungs.sh` logs a successful probe. The run's primary held-out metric would read NaN at every rung with
nothing anywhere saying why -- 08:07 binding 1 in its worst form. **Not active right now**: the init run finished
(265/384 kept, the `GOLD HINTS` headline printed, process exited), so the cache is complete and valid. The guard
should be `os.path.getsize(HINTS) > 0` plus a write-to-temp-and-rename, or a count printed beside every result.
I left the file alone because the interactive session was executing it; it is a two-line fix for whoever owns it next.

**(2) WITH THE NOISE STATISTIC REMOVED, THE GATE QUESTION IS THE SAME QUESTION AS "DO THOUGHTS HELP" -- EXACTLY,
NOT APPROXIMATELY.** For a ranker at chance, achieved precision = the base rate pi, and
`p* - pi = -E[g] / (E[g|help] - E[g|hurt])`, because `E[g] = (E[g|help] - E[g|hurt]) (pi - p*)`. Verified to four
decimals at all three rungs: **0.2605 vs 0.2604** (rung 1), **0.2074 vs 0.2073** (rung 3), **0.2295 vs 0.2292**
(rung 5). **So 14:07 item (2) and the 14:24 addendum -- "the bar came down and the shortfall halved" -- were NOT
independent evidence of progress: that is the mean k=1 gain rising, divided by a shrinking spread. Two of the three
numbers I led with at 14:07 were one number.**
**And `p* = r/(1+r)` with `r = -E[g|hurt]/E[g|help]` the harm/help asymmetry, so `p*` is SCALE-FREE and FLOORS AT
0.50.** r: init 3.1 -> **1.72 / 1.61 / 1.64** at rungs 1/3/5. No amount of reader insensitivity takes the bar below
0.50, while the prize shrinks with the scale (ORACLE nats at q=0.23 **+0.84 / +0.79 / +0.77**). **The limit of this
trajectory is the trivial point -- thoughts neither help nor hurt, bar equals base rate, selection buys exactly
zero. So the 14:07 "race between a falling bar and the achievable signal" is the WRONG frame and is withdrawn: the
bar and the prize fall together. The only two independent quantities left are the MEAN GAIN and the DISCRIMINATION.**

**WHY IT FAILED, AND WHY THE HONEST READING IS BETTER NEWS THAN MY FORECAST.** "Best over q" picks the
operating point **in sample, per rung**, from seven correlated estimates whose error bars differ **6x**
(+-0.0280 at q=0.20 vs **+-0.1038** at q=0.01 for rung 1). The noisiest cells win the max most often, so
early rungs are handed a value they have not earned -- rung 1's "best" is q=0.01, one percent of 1,516
anchors. **At a FIXED q=0.20, chosen once and never re-chosen, the series is**

**WHY, DIAGNOSED RATHER THAN GUESSED, AND IT COST ONE MORE SCRIPT.** Two reasons, and the first was my own bug.

**(1) THE FIRST DIAGNOSIS WAS ITSELF WRONG BECAUSE OF A SILENT KEY FAILURE -- G181.** I wrote `agent/scratchpad/anchorpair_1008_1007.py` to pair on the *anchor* rather than the sequence, keying on `(set, seq, r.get("pos", r.get("i", -1)))`. **The records have neither `pos` nor `i`.** Every anchor in a sequence therefore collapsed to the key `(set, seq, -1)` and last-write-wins reduced **1,536 anchors per rung to 48 rows**. The script ran clean, printed "948 anchors above H>4.0 at every rung" as **"48 (union 48)"** -- a number that should have been impossible to believe for one second, since each file has 1,536 rows -- and produced a confident, publishable-looking **null: fixed-position slope -0.0232 +- 0.0555, t -0.42, "0.30 of anchors positive"**. Had I printed less, I would have filed "the trend disappears when you freeze the positions" as a finding. **The schema check that fixed it: the position field is `n` (anchor index into the sequence, range 32-1006), and `(set, seq, n)` is unique with exactly 1,536 keys = 48 sequences x 32 positions per file.** **Rule: a join key is never defaulted. Assert it exists, and print the distinct-key count against the design's expected value before using it.** Family with G173/G177/G179 -- the fourth distinct way a free choice inside a statistic has invented a result in four ticks, except this one was not a choice, it was a typo with a fallback.

**(2) G180 IS HALF WRONG, AND THE WRONG HALF IS EXACTLY WHAT MADE PAIRING LOOK EASY.** G180 says "the 48 sequences and 32 positions/rung are fixed". The **sequences** are fixed. The **positions are not**: `(set, seq, n)` keys overlap **1,280 / 1,536** between rung 190 and rung 2470, and only **948 of 2,225** union anchors clear H>4.0 at **all 12** rungs. The probe re-picks its positions per checkpoint (they are entropy-selected, and entropy moves with the model). So a paired design must either restrict to the 948 survivors or accept a leaky join; "pair on the sequence" pairs 46 noisy ~6.6-anchor means and pays the within-cluster noise that pooling would have averaged away. **G180's determinism claim stands (max |gain1 difference| 0.000e+00 on the shared checkpoint); its fixed-design claim is amended here.**

**(3) THE REAL REASON PAIRING CANNOT WIN HERE -- G182.** With the key fixed, the anchor-paired estimator on the 948 survivors gives **+0.0241 +- 0.0123** (sequence-clustered), **+-0.0114** if treated as i.i.d. over the 190 selected anchors -- i.e. **within 1% of the unpaired 0.0122, and clustering inflates it only 1.09x.** Yet the across-rung correlation of a given anchor's `gain1` is **+0.86** (adjacent rungs 0.87-0.93), which is high. Both are true because the per-anchor reading is **one sampled thought, redrawn at every rung**: per-anchor sd across rungs **0.218**, which over a 2.28k-step lever arm scatters the per-anchor slope by **+-0.157**. **Pairing removes the between-anchor level variance; it cannot remove noise that is redrawn at every measurement.** The binding constraint is the probe's **anchor count** (190 at q=0.20 of 948 survivors), not the estimator: se < 0.0085 needs roughly **twice** the anchors, i.e. the ceiling probe widened from **48 sequences to ~100**. **No further tick should spend effort on cleverer statistics for this quantity; widen the probe or quote +-0.012.**

**G183, THE SUBSTANTIVE RESULT, AND IT IS THE STRONGEST FORM THE PRICE TAG HAS TAKEN.** The 08:07 slope let the gate **re-rank every rung**, so a sceptic can say the trend is the gate learning to avoid hard positions rather than the thoughts improving. Test: freeze **both**. Fixed set = top **q=0.20** by `gate_pre` **at rung 190 alone** (the first rung, chosen once, named per G179) among the 948 anchors above H>4.0 at every rung -> **190 anchors in 39 sequences**, followed across all 12 rungs:
**-0.1128 -0.0710 -0.0623 -0.0494 -0.0436 -0.0636 -0.0567 -0.0414 -0.0364 -0.0377 -0.0246 -0.0554**.

**How I got here.** The 13:41 rung-1 line recorded the held-out gold-hint arm across runs 97-98 as +0.10 (3230) ->
-0.08 (3610) -> -0.23 (3990) -> -0.29 (4180) and called it "the reader's held-out use of a correct hint DECAYING".
Before writing that a fourth time I read what the teacher actually says. `agent/hint_gen.py` prompts a 3B instruct
model for "at most 12 words that describe what comes next ... WITHOUT using any of the next words themselves, their
inflections, or any numbers that appear in them", then **drops any hint containing a content word (>=4 letters or a
digit run) of the span** -- 384 generations in, 265 survive, so the filter removes 31% and it removes exactly the
informative ones. What survives is **4.8 tokens long** (median 5, max 8, measured over all 58,566 pool rows and all
265 held-out rows, i.e. 60% of the 8-token thought slot), and at entropy-triggered anchors -- which in this corpus
are disproportionately names, markup, numbers and discourse boundaries -- it says things like:

    span "OlderDan\nHomework Helper\napp said:\nOh, ok. I"           hint "Response to previous explanation"
    span "Anyway, thanks a lot for helping. and please do tell me"   hint "consequences of interactions here"
    span " common acceleration of B and C.\n\nOlderDan\nHomework..." hint "resultant motion of connected objects"

**The measurement.** `runs/probes/thoughts/heldout_hints_verbatim.jsonl` (built by
`agent/scratchpad/mk_verbatim_hints_1407.py`) holds the SAME 265 (set, seq, n) rows -- key asserted unique and
identical in both arms, G181 -- with the hint replaced by the **first L=8 true target tokens** taken straight from
the data memmaps with `hint_eval.py`'s own `T_OPEN/T_CLOSE -> 220` mapping applied, so the two arms differ in the
hint text and in nothing else: same anchors, same inserted-text geometry, same scorer, same model.

                      paraphrase          verbatim-first-8      paired diff        helps

**So the thing runs 96-98 were calling the ceiling is not a ceiling.** It is a near-zero-information teacher, and
the correct description of the training is not "the reader goes deaf" or "the arm decays" but **"training moves the
reader from -5.30 (catastrophically harmed by an uninformative thought, untrained) to about zero (correctly ignoring
it), and then has nowhere left to go"**. The five-rung series -0.08, +0.02, -0.00, +0.10, -0.08 and run 98's -0.23,

                                                tokens 9-16  -3.240 +-0.192 (helps 10%)

**The channel pays for exactly what the thought spells out and then costs 3.2 nats.** My first draft of this tick's
conclusion -- "the reader is fine, the teacher was the problem, so give it a teacher that names the future" -- was
half wrong, and the run I had already written a config for (`runs/think99_goldspan/config.sh`, a gold-span teacher)
would have trained a reader to **copy**, which is a skill the writer can never exploit at inference because at
inference nothing names the future. **The design is held, not launched, and the config now carries this number.**
Note too that the next-token gain is **-0.078**: even with the answer sitting in its own bracket the untrained model
does not copy the FIRST token (it has no aligning prefix yet); the copying starts at token 2.

**G188 -- THE TRAINED READER HAS LEARNED TO TURN THE THOUGHT CHANNEL *DOWN*, AND THAT IS THE MECHANISM BEHIND THE
WHOLE HINT LINE.** The same verbatim-first-8 arm, same 265 anchors, read by **run 98's rung-4 weights (step 4,750)**
instead of the init (`runs/probes/hintceiling/verbatim_r98_4750.*`):

                                    untrained init          run 98 step 4,750
        next token              -0.078 +-0.191            +0.219 +-0.068   (helps 56% -> 60%)
        tokens 1-8 (named)     +12.751 +-0.689            +5.177 +-0.318   (helps 86% -> 91%)
        tokens 9-16 (not)       -3.240 +-0.192            -0.301 +-0.064   (helps 10% -> 40%)
        16 tokens               +9.511 +-1.113            +4.876 +-0.323

**Training cut the gain from a literally correct thought by 59% (+12.75 -> +5.18) and cut the collateral damage
beyond it by 91% (-3.24 -> -0.30).** That is exactly what a reader SHOULD do after 2,300 steps in which every thought
it saw was uninformative: attenuate the channel. It is also the worst possible preparation for a thought that is
worth something -- and it is not a small effect, it is more than half the available gain, destroyed. Note the gain
is each model's own clean CE minus its own thought CE, and the trained model's clean CE on these spans is HIGHER
(base damage +0.044), which would inflate its gain, so the 59% cut is if anything understated. **Consequence for
every future design on this line: the teacher must be informative from step 0. Training on uninformative thoughts
does not leave the channel idle, it closes it.**

**WHAT THE PROGRAMME'S REMAINING QUESTION IS, STATED SO IT CANNOT BE FUDGED.** A thought the model writes from its
own context carries no information the context does not already carry -- by the data-processing inequality the only
thing a self-written thought can buy is **serial computation at the anchor**. G187 says the channel pays only for
what the thought NAMES. Put together, there is exactly one surviving route: **the model drafts the next k tokens and
is scored on those same k tokens**, and it pays only if writing the continuation out beats predicting it in one
shot. That is self-speculative thinking, it needs no training to test, and **it has never been measured**: the
ceiling probe samples at temp 1.0 from an RL-trained writer, which is a different object from a greedy draft.
**Launched this tick on CPU** (`agent/scratchpad/probe_greedy_1407.py`, a copy of `probe_ceiling.py` with two edits
-- absolute `sys.path` and `$GREEDY_TEMP` instead of the hardcoded 1.0 -- so the live loop's copy is untouched):

you ever write "nothing enforces X", `grep -n "stop_run" agent/running/mon*<run>*.sh`. Killing the `run_think.sh`

bracket.** Both arms fell by ~0.5 nats because the slot itself got more expensive, and the reader's ability to tell

other way round and small (price -0.041 +-0.026, sensitivity -0.125 +-0.033, t -3.7). The 14:40 write-up compared

sensitivity is real and large (+5.5 nats over 16 tokens) and it is still **entirely** a copying channel -- it pays
for the 8 tokens the thought names and nothing after them -- which is G187, and G187 is why a gold-span teacher is
useless at inference.

**G210(a) -- THE STOP-RULE DEFECT, AND IT IS A NEW KIND FOR THIS CLASS.** `agent/etrig_monitor.sh` skips D2's `rep_kept` clause on any run that logs `r_std` (the hintmix family does, so it was off for **all 1,403 of run 98's steps**) and justifies it in its own comment: *"Collapse is still caught, on ALL generated thoughts, by digit_share/open_share."* That comment **names `think_grpo.py`**, and `think_grpo.py:469/471` index `Z[0, a]` -- sample 0 of G=8. The six-trainer audit:

      think_entropy.py   Z[a]      one thought per anchor -- ALL watched. TRUE here, and ONLY here.
      think_grpo.py      Z[0, a]   | think_grpo_gate.py Z[0, a] | think_oracle.py Z[0, a]
      think_bestof.py    Z[0, a]   (its rep_kept reads the SELECTED best -- correct there)
      think_hintmix.py   Zo[0, a]  all three, on a family that KEEPS NOTHING, so "rep_kept" is a misnomer too

**WHAT IT COSTS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT -- AND I NEARLY OVERCLAIMED THIS.** `digit_share` is a MEAN over thoughts, so sample 0 is an **unbiased** estimator with G-fold variance; nothing to correct. `open_share` is a **MODAL** share, and a modal share over m items cannot fall below 1/m, so reading 1 of G lifts its floor from 1/(G*n_valid) to **1/n_valid**:

      run 90 (no collapse)  0.1312  floor 0.1256   100% of   207 rows within 0.02 of the floor
      run 95 (no collapse)  0.1671  floor 0.1673   100% of 1,288 rows within 0.02
      run 98 (no collapse)  0.1710  floor 0.1673   100% of 1,403 rows within 0.02
      run 89 (COLLAPSED)    0.128 -> 0.99 = 7.9x its floor | run 85 -> 0.699 | run 84 -> 0.183

**The detector is NOT broken** -- ~6x headroom from floor to bar, and it caught runs 89 and 85. What is wrong is **reading a low value as a measurement of diversity**: it is the statistic's arithmetic minimum. It is additionally mis-normalised (numerator skips micros with <=1 valid anchor, divisor is `n_micro`), and **5.7% of run-98 rows sit at or BELOW their own floor, which a true modal share cannot do** -- that is the drag, made visible. Its exact size is unmeasurable because **think_hintmix emits neither `n_micro` nor `n_rco` nor `n_hvalid`**.

**G210(b) -- THE TICK'S RESEARCH RESULT: WHY HINT-RL COULD NOT WORK, FROM ITS OWN POPULATION** (`dumps.jsonl`, 56 hint spots, `agent/scratchpad/suppress_1207.out`):

      gold hint helps                          94.6% of spots  (+5.171 nats, K=16 span)
      the writer's OWN thoughts help           82.1% of spots  (+2.819 nats)
      own SAMPLES beating the hint              13.4%          -> >= 86.6% get a NEGATIVE advantage
      own helps AND none of six beats the hint  62.5% (35/56)  -- every one pushed DOWN
      where that happens, the hint wins by      +2.352 nats

**A REWARD DEFINED AS A MARGIN AGAINST A BETTER TEACHER HAS NO WAY TO SAY "HELPFUL, BUT WORSE THAN GOLD", SO IT SUPPRESSES MOST OF WHAT THE WRITER GETS RIGHT.** A mechanism for run 98's existing futility verdict -- **NOT an eighth negative result; G205's count stays at seven.** Consistent with G208 (39% of own thoughts help at deployment anchors, nothing label-free finds them). **CAVEAT PRINTED WHEREVER IT IS QUOTED:** pool-block anchors chosen because a gold paraphrase exists, K=16 SPAN totals, versus -0.217 nats per thought at deployment anchors. **The two populations must never be pooled.**

**G210(c) -- THE OTHER FOUR.** `best_helps` on hintmix = `(max over G=8 own samples > 0)`, an **ORACLE** over samples nothing selects (0.605 vs `helps` 0.403, ratio 1.50, >= helps on all 1,403 rows); the SAME NAME on `think_bestof` is deployable, because there the design does select. `hrl_adv` = mean of `clip((own gain - the HINT's gain)/sd_own, +-3)`: dimensionless, centred on the TEACHER not the group mean, so **not mean-zero like a GRPO advantage** -- near 0 means "own == hint", not "no signal" -- and read BEFORE the `--neg-scale` asymmetry that enters the loss (negative on 1,403/1,403 blocks, mean -1.85, last-100 -2.10 against the -3.0 clip). `n_hints` is `n_hvalid` **undivided**: a raw count, 306-358, and the exact denominator of every hint-arm mean in its own record. `hint_helps`/`hint_helps1` are the span and k=1 rates, printed as a bare "96%/79%" slash.

`s_j = sum_k (ce_clean[k] - ce_span[j][k])` -- the reward's own horizon, no per-position re-selection. Baseline =
**mean-of-six** (a random draft's expectation), headroom = **UNCLAMPED** best-of-six minus mean-of-six, because a
selector must emit what it picks and cannot fall back to silence. 48 sequence clusters pooled across rungs.
CV = **leave-one-SET-out** (4 folds, disjoint sequences and disjoint text) rather than the prior's
leave-one-rung-out, which shares anchors across folds. Scripts/outputs `agent/scratchpad/picker98_0407.{py,out}`
